import Mathlib

structure CycleGraph where
  adj : Array (Array Nat)

def CycleGraph.well_formed (g : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.adj.size →
    ∀ v, v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → v < g.adj.size

def CycleGraph.size (g : CycleGraph) : Nat :=
  g.adj.size

def CycleGraph.has_edge (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) : Prop :=
  u < g.adj.size ∧
  v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[]

def CycleGraph.is_path (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  p.length > 0 ∧
  ∀ i, i + 1 < p.length →
    g.has_edge (p.getD i 0) (p.getD (i + 1) 0)

def CycleGraph.is_cycle (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  g.is_path p ∧ p.length > 1 ∧ p.head? = p.getLast?

def CycleGraph.graph_has_cycle (g : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, g.is_cycle p

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def has_cycle_precond (graph : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  graph.well_formed
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Successors of `u`, as a list. -/
def CycleGraph.succList (g : CycleGraph) (u : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList

/-- `g.iter k` is the list of all nodes that are the endpoint of some walk
consisting of exactly `k` edges (starting from an arbitrary node of the graph). -/
def CycleGraph.iter (g : CycleGraph) : Nat → List Nat
  | 0 => List.range g.adj.size
  | k + 1 => (g.iter k).flatMap g.succList

/-- A walk of `k` edges, described by its vertex enumeration `f`. -/
def CycleGraph.IsWalk (g : CycleGraph) (k : Nat) (f : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, i < k → g.has_edge (f i) (f (i + 1))) ∧ (∀ i, i ≤ k → f i < g.adj.size)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def has_cycle (graph : CycleGraph)
    (h_precond : has_cycle_precond graph) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  !(graph.iter graph.adj.size).isEmpty
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def has_cycle_postcond (graph : CycleGraph) (result : Bool)
    (_ : has_cycle_precond graph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result = graph.graph_has_cycle
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem mem_succList_iff (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) :
    v ∈ g.succList u ↔ v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] := by
  simp [CycleGraph.succList]

theorem head?_getD (l : List Nat) (h : l ≠ []) : l.head? = some (l.getD 0 0) := by
  cases l with
  | nil => exact absurd rfl h
  | cons a t => simp

theorem getLast?_getD (l : List Nat) (h : l ≠ []) :
    l.getLast? = some (l.getD (l.length - 1) 0) := by
  have hpos : 0 < l.length := by
    cases l with
    | nil => exact absurd rfl h
    | cons a t => simp
  have hb : l.length - 1 < l.length := by omega
  rw [List.getLast?_eq_getElem?, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hb]
  congr 1
  rw [List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ hb]

theorem getD_map_range_add (f : Nat → Nat) (i m t : Nat) (ht : t < m) :
    ((List.range m).map (fun k => f (i + k))).getD t 0 = f (i + t) := by
  simp [ht]

/-- The endpoints of `k`-edge walks are exactly the elements of `g.iter k`. -/
theorem mem_iter_iff (g : CycleGraph) (hg : g.well_formed) :
    ∀ (k v : Nat), v ∈ g.iter k ↔ ∃ f, g.IsWalk k f ∧ f k = v := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v
    constructor
    · intro h
      simp only [CycleGraph.iter, List.mem_range] at h
      exact ⟨fun _ => v, ⟨fun i hi => absurd hi (by omega), fun i _ => h⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
      simp only [CycleGraph.iter, List.mem_range]
      exact hf.2 0 (le_refl 0)
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v
    constructor
    · intro h
      simp only [CycleGraph.iter, List.mem_flatMap] at h
      obtain ⟨u, hu, hv⟩ := h
      obtain ⟨f, hf, hfk⟩ := (ih u).1 hu
      have hu_lt : u < g.adj.size := by rw [← hfk]; exact hf.2 k (le_refl k)
      have hv_mem : v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] := (mem_succList_iff g u v).1 hv
      have hv_lt : v < g.adj.size := hg u hu_lt v hv_mem
      refine ⟨fun i => if i = k + 1 then v else f i, ⟨?_, ?_⟩, by simp⟩
      · intro i hi
        rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i k with hik | hik
        · have h1 : i ≠ k + 1 := by omega
          have h2 : i + 1 ≠ k + 1 := by omega
          simp only [if_neg h1, if_neg h2]
          exact hf.1 i hik
        · have hik' : i = k := by omega
          have h1 : i ≠ k + 1 := by omega
          have h2 : i + 1 = k + 1 := by omega
          simp only [if_neg h1, if_pos h2]
          rw [hik', hfk]
          exact ⟨hu_lt, hv_mem⟩
      · intro i hi
        by_cases h1 : i = k + 1
        · simp only [if_pos h1]
          exact hv_lt
        · simp only [if_neg h1]
          exact hf.2 i (by omega)
    · rintro ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
      simp only [CycleGraph.iter, List.mem_flatMap]
      refine ⟨f k, (ih (f k)).2 ⟨f, ⟨fun i hi => hf.1 i (by omega),
        fun i hi => hf.2 i (by omega)⟩, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
      exact (mem_succList_iff g (f k) (f (k + 1))).2 (hf.1 k (by omega)).2

/-- A walk that revisits a vertex (`f i = f j`, `i < j`) contains a cycle. -/
theorem cycle_of_repeat (g : CycleGraph) (f : Nat → Nat) (i j : Nat)
    (hij : i < j) (hedge : ∀ t, i ≤ t → t < j → g.has_edge (f t) (f (t + 1)))
    (heq : f i = f j) : g.graph_has_cycle := by
  refine ⟨(List.range (j - i + 1)).map (fun k => f (i + k)), ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · simp
  · intro t ht
    simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range] at ht
    rw [getD_map_range_add f i (j - i + 1) t (by omega),
        getD_map_range_add f i (j - i + 1) (t + 1) (by omega)]
    exact hedge (i + t) (by omega) (by omega)
  · simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range]
    omega
  · rw [head?_getD _ (by simp), getLast?_getD _ (by simp)]
    simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range]
    have h7 : j - i + 1 - 1 = j - i := by omega
    rw [h7, getD_map_range_add f i (j - i + 1) 0 (by omega),
        getD_map_range_add f i (j - i + 1) (j - i) (by omega)]
    have h8 : i + (j - i) = j := by omega
    rw [h8, Nat.add_zero, heq]

/-- A cycle can be traversed repeatedly, giving walks of every length. -/
theorem walk_of_cycle (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) (hp : g.is_cycle p) :
    ∀ n, ∃ f, g.IsWalk n f := by
  have hedge := hp.1.2
  have hlen1 : p.length > 1 := hp.2.1
  have hhl := hp.2.2
  have hne : p ≠ [] := by
    intro h
    rw [h] at hlen1
    simp at hlen1
  have hcyc : p.getD (p.length - 1) 0 = p.getD 0 0 := by
    have h := (head?_getD p hne).symm.trans (hhl.trans (getLast?_getD p hne))
    exact (Option.some.inj h).symm
  have hm : 0 < p.length - 1 := by omega
  have hkey : ∀ k, g.has_edge (p.getD (k % (p.length - 1)) 0)
      (p.getD ((k + 1) % (p.length - 1)) 0) := by
    intro k
    have hr : k % (p.length - 1) < p.length - 1 := Nat.mod_lt _ hm
    have hedge' : g.has_edge (p.getD (k % (p.length - 1)) 0)
        (p.getD (k % (p.length - 1) + 1) 0) := hedge (k % (p.length - 1)) (by omega)
    have hd : (p.length - 1) * (k / (p.length - 1)) + k % (p.length - 1) = k :=
      Nat.div_add_mod k (p.length - 1)
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge (k % (p.length - 1) + 1) (p.length - 1) with hc | hc
    · have hmod : (k + 1) % (p.length - 1) = k % (p.length - 1) + 1 := by
        have he : k + 1 = (k % (p.length - 1) + 1) + (p.length - 1) * (k / (p.length - 1)) := by
          omega
        rw [he, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_left, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hc]
      rw [hmod]
      exact hedge'
    · have hc' : k % (p.length - 1) + 1 = p.length - 1 := by omega
      have hmod : (k + 1) % (p.length - 1) = 0 := by
        have he : k + 1 = (p.length - 1) * (k / (p.length - 1) + 1) := by
          rw [Nat.mul_succ]; omega
        rw [he, Nat.mul_mod_right]
      rw [hc'] at hedge'
      rw [hmod, ← hcyc]
      exact hedge'
  intro n
  exact ⟨fun k => p.getD (k % (p.length - 1)) 0,
    ⟨fun i _ => hkey i, fun i _ => (hkey i).1⟩⟩
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem has_cycle_postcond_satisfied (graph : CycleGraph)
    (h_precond : has_cycle_precond graph) :
    has_cycle_postcond graph (has_cycle graph h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  simp only [has_cycle_postcond, has_cycle]
  rw [eq_iff_iff]
  constructor
  · -- soundness: a nonempty `iter n` yields a walk with `n` edges, hence a repeat
    intro h
    have hne : graph.iter graph.adj.size ≠ [] := by
      intro he
      rw [he] at h
      simp at h
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ : ∃ v, v ∈ graph.iter graph.adj.size := by
      cases hcase : graph.iter graph.adj.size with
      | nil => exact absurd hcase hne
      | cons a t => exact ⟨a, by simp⟩
    obtain ⟨f, hf, -⟩ := (mem_iter_iff graph h_precond _ v).1 hv
    have hcard : (Finset.range graph.adj.size).card
        < (Finset.range (graph.adj.size + 1)).card := by simp
    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ Finset.range (graph.adj.size + 1),
        f a ∈ Finset.range graph.adj.size := by
      intro a ha
      simp only [Finset.mem_range] at ha ⊢
      exact hf.2 a (by omega)
    obtain ⟨x, hx, y, hy, hxy, hfxy⟩ :=
      Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to hcard hmaps
    simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hx hy
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge x y with hlt | hge
    · exact cycle_of_repeat graph f x y hlt (fun t _ ht2 => hf.1 t (by omega)) hfxy
    · exact cycle_of_repeat graph f y x (by omega)
        (fun t _ ht2 => hf.1 t (by omega)) hfxy.symm
  · -- completeness: a cycle can be unrolled into a walk with `n` edges
    intro h
    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := h
    obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := walk_of_cycle graph p hp graph.adj.size
    have hmem : f graph.adj.size ∈ graph.iter graph.adj.size :=
      (mem_iter_iff graph h_precond _ _).2 ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
    cases hcase : graph.iter graph.adj.size with
    | nil =>
      rw [hcase] at hmem
      simp at hmem
    | cons a t => simp
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What I did

**Implementation** (`code` region):
```lean
!(graph.iter graph.adj.size).isEmpty
```
where `iter` (in `auxcode`) computes endpoints of walks of a given edge-length:
`iter 0 = List.range n`, `iter (k+1) = (iter k).flatMap succList`.

The correctness hinge: *a graph on `n` nodes has a cycle iff some walk with exactly `n` edges exists*. Since `iter` recurses structurally on the step count, termination is immediate — no visited-set well-foundedness argument is needed, even though cycles make naive DFS diverge.

**Proof** (`lemma` + `proof` regions), all in terms of walks-as-functions `f : Nat → Nat` (extending a walk is then just an `if`, rather than list-append index juggling):

- `mem_iter_iff` — `v ∈ g.iter k ↔ ∃ f, IsWalk k f ∧ f k = v`, by induction on `k`. The successor step uses `well_formed` to keep the new endpoint in range.
- `cycle_of_repeat` — soundness. If `f i = f j` with `i < j`, the segment `(List.range (j-i+1)).map (fun k => f (i+k))` satisfies `is_cycle`: length `> 1`, consecutive `has_edge`, and `head? = getLast?` since `f i = f j`.
- `walk_of_cycle` — completeness. Given a cycle `p` of `m = p.length - 1` edges, `fun k => p.getD (k % m) 0` is a walk of *every* length; the wrap-around case `k % m + 1 = m` is closed by `p.getD (p.length-1) 0 = p.getD 0 0`, extracted from `head? = getLast?`.
- Main theorem: `→` gets a walk of `n` edges whose `n+1` vertices all lie in `range n`, so `Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to` gives a repeat, then `cycle_of_repeat`; `←` unrolls the cycle to length `n` and concludes `iter n ≠ []`.
